lines.raw: Health plans express almost every number **per member per month** (for money), **per 1,000 members per year** (for how often things happen) or **per unit** (for the price of one thing), so that groups of any size and any length of time can be compared.
lines.say: Health plans express almost every number per member per month (for money), per 1,000 members per year (for how often things happen) or per unit (for the price of one thing), so that groups of any size and any length of time can be compared.

lines.raw: 10,000 people covered all year = 10,000 × 12 = **120,000 member months**.

scenes.section: The US version: three kinds of rate

lines.raw: The three standard rates.
lines.say: The three standard rates.

lines.raw: **PMPM** (per member per month). Formula: Dollars ÷ member months. Used for: Money: cost, premium. Typical question: "How much do we spend on each member each month?".
lines.say: P M P M (per member per month). Formula: Dollars ÷ member months. Used for: Money: cost, premium. Typical question: "How much do we spend on each member each month?".

lines.raw: **PMPY** (per member per year). Formula: PMPM × 12. Used for: Money, when people think in years. Typical question: "What does a member cost us in a year?".
lines.say: P M P Y (per member per year). Formula: P M P M × 12. Used for: Money, when people think in years. Typical question: "What does a member cost us in a year?".

lines.raw: **Per 1,000** (per 1,000 members per year). Formula: Events ÷ member months × 12,000. Used for: How often things happen: admissions, visits. Typical question: "How many hospital stays do we see for every 1,000 members?".
lines.say: Per 1,000 (per 1,000 members per year). Formula: Events ÷ member months × 12,000. Used for: How often things happen: admissions, visits. Typical question: "How many hospital stays do we see for every 1,000 members?".

lines.raw: **Per unit** (per visit, per admission, per script). Formula: Dollars ÷ number of units. Used for: Price of one thing. Typical question: "What does one hospital stay cost us on average?".
lines.say: Per unit (per visit, per admission, per script). Formula: Dollars ÷ number of units. Used for: Price of one thing. Typical question: "What does one hospital stay cost us on average?".

scenes.section: The US version: three kinds of rate

lines.raw: PMPM.
lines.say: P M P M.

lines.raw: PMPM equals Total dollars ÷ Member months.
lines.say: P M P M equals Total dollars ÷ Member months.

lines.raw: For example: Lone Star Health paid $46,920,000 in claims over 120,000 member months: $46,920,000 ÷ 120,000 equals $391.00 PMPM.
lines.say: For example: Lone Star Health paid 46920000 dollars in claims over 120,000 member months: 46920000 dollars ÷ 120,000 equals 391 dollars P M P M.

lines.raw: PMPY equals $391.00 times 12 equals $4,692.
lines.say: P M P Y equals 391 dollars times 12 equals 4692 dollars.

scenes.section: The US version: three kinds of rate

lines.raw: Rate per 1,000 members per year.
lines.say: Rate per 1,000 members per year.

lines.raw: Rate per 1,000 equals Events ÷ Member months times 12,000.
lines.say: Rate per 1,000 equals Events ÷ Member months times 12,000.

lines.raw: For example: 720 hospital admissions over 120,000 member months: 720 ÷ 120,000 times 12,000 equals 72 admissions per 1,000 members per year.
lines.say: For example: 720 hospital admissions over 120,000 member months: 720 ÷ 120,000 times 12,000 equals 72 admissions per 1,000 members per year.

scenes.section: The US version: three kinds of rate

lines.raw: Dividing member months by 12 gives **average members**.
lines.say: Dividing member months by 12 gives average members.

lines.raw: Multiplying by 1,000 gives "per 1,000 members".
lines.say: Multiplying by 1,000 gives "per 1,000 members".

lines.raw: This also **annualizes** the rate: it always means "per 1,000 members **per year**", even if you only have 3 months of data.
lines.say: This also annualizes the rate: it always means "per 1,000 members per year", even if you only have 3 months of data.

scenes.section: The US version: three kinds of rate

lines.raw: Per unit.
lines.say: Per unit.

lines.raw: Cost per unit equals Total dollars for that service ÷ Number of units.
lines.say: Cost per unit equals Total dollars for that service ÷ Number of units.

lines.raw: For example: $12,960,000 spent on 720 hospital admissions: $12,960,000 ÷ 720 equals $18,000 per admission.
lines.say: For example: 12960000 dollars spent on 720 hospital admissions: 12960000 dollars ÷ 720 equals 18000 dollars per admission.

lines.raw: Unit.

lines.raw: **Paid PMPM** is the plan's own cost.
